cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The search term, sort column, direction and limit taken off the query string are concatenated straight into the SQL text handed to prisma.$queryRawUnsafe; escaping the LIKE wildcards does nothing for the surrounding quotes and the ORDER BY clause is unquoted, so a public search request can append arbitrary SQL that runs with the API's database role.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The same hand-written aggregate, but the search term is bound as a Prisma.sql parameter and the ORDER BY fragment is picked out of the SORT_FRAGMENTS allowlist, so no request value ever reaches the query text; the rows are additionally scoped to the caller's organiserId.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The transfer resolves the ticket from the path id alone and never compares ticket.ownerId with identity.accountId, so any authenticated attendee can hand somebody else's ticket to an address they control; the only checks made are on event and ticket state.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The same path-id-addressed ticket mutation, but it runs as an updateMany whose where clause carries ownerId: actor.accountId, so a ticket belonging to another account matches nothing and the zero count is returned as a 404 — the ownership predicate is the guard.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: readScannedPass splits the compact pass token and JSON.parses its claim segment without ever recomputing the HMAC that readPassToken in src/lib/identity.ts exists to check, so ticketId, eventId and exp all come from an unauthenticated string and a hand-crafted QR code is admitted and written to the gate scan log as a valid pass.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The same `<claims>.<signature>` compact token shape, but readSignedToken recomputes the HMAC over the claim segment and compares it with timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers before a single claim is decoded, and only then applies the expiry check, so a forged or edited token is rejected.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The wildcard segment params['*'] is joined onto env.statementDir and opened with Bun.file with no containment or allowlist check, so a request like GET /api/organiser/payouts/exports/../../../../etc/passwd streams a file from outside the statement tree back to any organiser account.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The same join + Bun.file download, but the relative key is read off the Payout row that was selected by organiserId, it has to match the generator's own naming pattern, and the resolved absolute path has to still sit under STATEMENT_ROOT before the file is opened.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The only guard on the group is requireAccount, and the create handler checks neither the caller's promoter role nor that body.eventId belongs to their organiser, so any signed-in attendee can mint a 100%-off code against any published event — the sibling read and revoke handlers in the same file do apply requirePromoter and an organiserId scope.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: body.amountCents is what decides whether the request auto-approves and is also the figure written to the credit note and incremented onto the account's wallet balance; it is never compared with ticket.pricePaidCents, so an attendee holding a cheap ticket can request the auto-approve ceiling and be credited far more than was ever captured.

cases.architecture: Elysia 1.3 on Bun with Prisma 6 for data access; caller identity comes from a bearer session token whose HMAC is verified in a scoped Elysia derive plugin (src/lib/identity.ts).
cases.why: The same credit-note and wallet write, but the amount is recomputed from ticket.pricePaidCents and the event's fee policy and requestedAmountCents is ignored for the ledger, and the request is only found when the reviewer is FINANCE staff at the organiser that owns the event.
